title: Classify the controls by type
scenario: Drop each control into the TYPE it belongs to. Type is about when the control acts relative to the incident, not what the control is made of. A security guard is physical in category and can be deterrent, preventive or detective in type depending on what they are there to do.
requirements: Every control goes in exactly one column.
Judge by mechanism, not by outcome: ask whether a determined attacker who ignores it is still stopped.

items.label: Isolating an unpatchable device on its own VLAN
Restoring a server from backup after ransomware

subtasks.correctNote: A vehicle physically cannot pass. Intent is irrelevant, which is what makes it preventive rather than deterrent.
It persuades and blocks nothing. The cameras it advertises are detective; the sign is deterrent.
It detects and alerts. An IPS would be preventive, because it sits inline and drops the traffic.
Backups repair after the event. Nothing about taking one prevents anything.
The control you wanted, patching, is impossible, so isolation meets the requirement another way. That substitution is what makes it compensating rather than merely preventive.
A policy instructs people what to do. Directive in type, managerial in category.
Makes an attacker feel exposed. It stops nobody who proceeds anyway.
A stolen password alone no longer works. The attack is stopped, not discouraged.
It tells you after the fact. Detective.
The incident happened and this repairs the damage. Corrective.
